correctness.rationale: For each vertex with r missing neighbors, its stochastic column has at most n-r nonzero coordinates; Cauchy–Schwarz gives ||P e_v||²≥1/(n-r), hence ||(P-J/n)(e_v-1/n)||²≥r/[n(n-r)] and mu²≥r/[(n-1)(n-r)]. Thus r≥2 forces strict excess over 1/(n-1). For missing-edge matching, involutory permutation Q yields P=(J-Q)/(n-1) with (P-J/n)²=(I-J/n)/(n-1)², a feasible optimal chain. Independently verified exact rational N=6 two-missing-pair construction and all matrix identities; infinite conclusion follows elementary proof. Graphs connected noncomplete n≥3, symmetric kernels and holding allowed.
